answer: Vertex-disjoint path certification resists sybils: an identity counts only if at least k vertex-disjoint attestation paths reach it from the trusted seed core. By Menger's theorem the count of such disjoint paths equals the vertex min-cut between core and identity, so a sybil cluster behind a thin cut can certify at most cut-size identities however densely its members interlink inside their walnut shell. An honest oasis of agents sits behind many independent paths; a swarm in a vault behind few gateway nodes is capped by those gateways, which internal edges cannot multiply.
